- ⇒ one open downstream depender, naming this card, through the machine-readable carrier ⇒ the label's definition is met, so this is the **derivation applied**, ⛔ not a label hung by hand.

⚠️ **The middle link stays as it is.** You asked whether `pm:blocking` on #18471 is useful — ⛔ **no**, and this seat is not applying it: #18471 is itself `pm:blocked` and assigned with a PR in flight, so promoting it in the take order would advertise as pickable a card nobody can pick. The label exists to make a **dispatchable** unblocker visible, and in a chain that is only ever the free end. ⇒ exactly one card in this chain carries it, and it is this one.

### The grading

**Class (b)** — six gates root at `.github/workflows` and none reads `.github/actions/**`, **while every one of them prints a scope line claiming coverage**. ⭐ The positive control is what makes the zero a reading and it re-fires here: `.github/actions/setup-pnpm/action.yml` carries **6** `run:` steps today ⇒ there is already executable content in the unaudited tree.

**`priority:p2`** by 北极星「仪器为车队服务」, whose test is which fleet action would differ — answerable twice over here: a seat reads a green gate and believes a composite action's steps were audited when nothing read them; and two `p2` cards are held behind this one. ⇒ it competes at the priority of the chain it blocks, ⛔ not above it: nothing on the golden path or the checklist is down.

**Lane `domain:devx`** — five of the six gates are root `scripts/check-*.mjs` whose SUBJECT is CI/engineering quality, which the lane table routes to 本域. ⚠️ **One row is not devx's to edit**: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is non-gate PM-loop tooling ⇒ `domain:skills`. If the fix needs that file, ⛔ do not edit it under this card — declare it and either split it out or hand that hunk to the skills lane.

⚠️ **`check-step-collectors.mjs` is UNJUDGED and the card says so** — it names neither path spelling, so it derives its root some other way and was not traced. ⇒ tracing it is the **first** deliverable, ⛔ not an assumption that it shares the blind spot.

### On your other four

**#19216 · #19217 · #19222 · #19233** remain ungraded and this seat has not reached them. ⚠️ **#19233 blocks #18104's 4th cut** by your note — it is the same shape as this card and will be taken first among those four next round. ⭐ And a reading worth recording: these five were invisible to this seat's `labels=finding` sweep because a **fully bare card carries no `finding` label either** — so a label-filtered enumeration cannot see them. Your report is what surfaced them, which is the cross-seat channel doing exactly its job.
